summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old female with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and chronic diastolic heart failure was admitted due to a headache and incidentally found hyperkalemia with a potassium level of 5.9 and ECG changes. She was treated with calcium gluconate and kayexelate, resulting in potassium normalization to 4.1. Her headache, a chronic issue related to left eye pain, resolved with oxycodone-acetaminophen. She underwent an inpatient hemodialysis session without complications. Warfarin dosing was adjusted due to subtherapeutic INR, and discharge medications were updated, including a change to sevelamer HCl. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and ophthalmologist.
